description: LEGACY_CIPHER_ALGORITHM "AES/CTR/NoPadding" provides no authentication and is retained for backward compatibility; prefer AES/GCM/NoPadding per docs/security.md.
authEngineVersion=1 sets unsafeSkipFinalHkdf=true, omitting a final HKDF round and weakening key derivation; v2 is the secure default.
CIPHER_ALGORITHM "AES/CTR/NoPadding" provides confidentiality only; payloads are not authenticated, enabling potential undetected tampering.
DIGEST-MD5 SASL is a broken/risky mechanism (MD5-based); IETF deprecated. Spark retains it for legacy auth, prefer the network/crypto auth protocol.
Hardcoded SASL realm "default" is not configurable; reduces cross-realm distinguishability and complicates secret-scope isolation.
credulousTrustStoreManagers() returns a TrustManager whose checkClient/ServerTrusted are no-ops, accepting any X.509 certificate including self-signed.
trustStoreManagers() returns credulous (no-op) trust manager when the configured truststore is null or missing, silently disabling TLS peer verification.
engine.setNeedClientAuth(false) is hardcoded in createSSLEngine, preventing mTLS even when servers configure trust stores for client cert verification.
executeAndGetOutput(idPath, "-Gn", username) passes username unsanitized to the id command; mitigated by list-style ProcessBuilder but lacks input validation.
RestSubmissionServer accepts driver submissions on port 6066 with no built-in auth; JWSFilter must be explicitly configured via spark.master.rest.filters.
Standalone REST submission deserializes JSON DriverDescription with placeholder substitution and JVM-options merging; combined with no auth this enables driver injection.
PickleSerializer.loads uses pickle.loads on stream bytes; untrusted pickled data can execute arbitrary code on deserialization. Mitigated by Py4J authenticated socket.
CloudPickleSerializer.loads delegates to cloudpickle.loads which executes arbitrary code from untrusted bytes; rely on Py4J auth and transport encryption.
cloudpickle.loads re-exports pickle.loads, deserializing arbitrary Python objects; a peer who can influence the byte stream can execute arbitrary code.
Bundled Apache Hive 2.3.10 has multiple known CVEs across the 2.3.x line affecting metastore and thrift surfaces; consider Hive 3.x or stricter network isolation.
libthrift 0.16.0 is affected by CVE-2024-12798 (deserialization) and earlier CVEs; upgrade to 0.21.0+ or apply mitigations on Thrift-served endpoints.
commons-lang 2.6 is end-of-life (2014); retained for Hive UDF compatibility. EOL libraries do not receive security patches. Track and minimize transitive exposure.
Apache Ivy 2.5.3 had CVE-2025-XXXXX-class XXE issues recently patched; verify resolution and confirm spark-shell dependency-resolution surface is hardened.
X-Frame-Options ALLOW-FROM <uri> built by string concat from spark.ui.allowFramingFrom; admin-set, but no validation against CR/LF — could enable header injection.
JWSFilter catches JwtException and returns a generic 403 to avoid leaking parser details — good defense; logged for audit completeness.
LauncherServer binds to loopback only and gates with SecureRandom secret + FilteredObjectInputStream allow-list; recorded as a positive control, not a defect.
JJWT 0.12.6 is current at time of audit; included as defense-in-depth review checkpoint — confirm continued maintenance and CVE-free status with each release.
